items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the cleared board); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The phase 6 objective gains a reach-quality term, so a road tier is something it can see
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-08: "Roads should be visible in phase 6 too." The ruling is written into GENERATION_STRATEGY.md as the objective's FIFTH TERM; this item is the work.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT FORCED IT (archived NR-793, confirmed on a live ten-market world, seed ABCDEF01, every term alive):
  tier=1  IN_REACH=25658  raws=122  composite=0.010256174
  tier=3  IN_REACH=26024  raws=122  composite=0.010256174
The reach frontier moves by 366 tiles. Every scored term is bit-identical.

THE CAUSE IS ONE NUMBER, and it is raws_in_reach: 122 either side. A road tier scales traversal COST, continuously. Terms 1 and 4 read reach through a PER-RESOURCE COVERAGE BOOLEAN - is there any reachable deposit of resource R in this catchment - and that boolean is SATURATED. With 122 resource-market pairs already covered across 25,658 tiles, 366 more tiles introduce no pair that was not already covered. So the axis moves a continuous quantity the objective only reads through a threshold, and the search spends a third of every round proposing a change it cannot score.

THE CONSTRAINT, and it is the whole difficulty. Cheaper traversal everywhere is trivially better, so a reach-quality term entered as a FLAT VIABILITY BONUS would reward a uniformly well-connected map - precisely the evenness term 3 and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Asymmetry is the deliverable exist to prevent. The term must be a PER-MARKET reading whose SPREAD is scored, exactly like terms 1 and 2, never a single global number added to the composite.

SLICE 1 IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A FEATURE, and it decides what the term reads. Two candidates: the mean traversal cost from a market to the tiles in its catchment, and the in-reach tile COUNT rather than the coverage boolean. Both are continuous and both move when a tier does. Score candidates that differ ONLY in road tier and ask whether the chosen reading DISCRIMINATES between them at all. A reading that does not is not worth keeping, and that is an afternoon's answer rather than a wasted build. This is § The first slice is the scorer applied to the new term.

TWO THINGS TO CARRY, both from the archived phase 6 work. (1) The default-seed phase 6 fixture is a TWO-MARKET world on which balance and composite evaluate to zero for every candidate - it is not a sound basis for any phase 6 measurement, and NR-793's first reading was taken on it before being re-run on a live world. Use a 10-15 market world. (2) Adding a term changes every ranking and therefore the selected landscape, so this is a world-moving change and owes the digest discipline in DELIVERY.md § The digest re-bless is one act per WAVE.

DONE WHEN: road tier 1, 2 and 3 produce DIFFERENT composites on a 10-15 market world; the difference is reported per market rather than as one global number; an even-reach landscape does not beat an uneven one at the same mean; and the determinism of the argmax is unchanged across thread counts.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the cleared board); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Re-measure the startup wait on the current base, and profile where the warm start actually goes
items.design:
FIRST, BECAUSE EVERY LATER DECISION IN THIS SPRINT IS TAKEN ON THIS NUMBER, and the number on record was measured on a line of history this base does not share.

WHAT WAS LAST RECORDED (archived BL-761, measured 2026-09-03 in the RELEASE play build, build_rel, with --autostart):
  epoch 1960 (two-span)  warm_start_80_ticks  73167 ms | convoys 14763.9 | run_economy_step 57023.9
  epoch 0    (ancient)   warm_start_80_ticks  72088 ms | convoys 28321.1 | run_economy_step 42361.6
Against app.cpp's own comment, which budgets "~25-38 s generation plus ~6 s warm start". That is 12x the budget, and it dwarfs generation's ~8 s.

TREAT THOSE AS A PRIOR, NOT AS FACT. They predate the current base by a substantial body of work. The first act of this item is to reproduce them here, in build_rel and NOT in build/ (Debug is a different world - the Debug warm start was recorded at ~11 minutes). If they no longer hold, that is the finding and the rest of the sprint is re-argued on the new figures rather than on these.

THEN PROFILE, because the split is the useful part and it differs by arc. run_economy_step dominates both but MORE on the industrial band; convoys are the reverse, with the ancient arc spending nearly twice as long moving goods. Everything else was noise (clear_markets ~0.11 s, apply_budget ~0.77 s, history_recorders ~0.39 s). Find what is O(n^2) or rebuilding per tick.

WHY IT IS NOT ONLY A LOADING-SCREEN PROBLEM: 42-57 s over 80 ticks is 530-710 ms PER TICK, which is also what the player pays per tick at speed once playing. This is a play-speed problem wearing a loading-screen costume, and that is the stronger reason to fix it.

DONE WHEN: the startup wait is measured on this base in the release build on both arcs, the per-pass split is recorded, and the dominant cost inside run_economy_step is named rather than guessed at.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the cleared board); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Retire the warm start and hand its burden to phase 6 - the position play opens on is SELECTED, not settled
items.design:
THE AIM, and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § The eight phases already carries it as design: phase 8 is retired and its burden moves to phase 6. The warm start is 80 undirected ticks that settle whatever generation happened to place; phase 6 is a directed search that CHOOSES the corporate landscape. Keeping both pays twice for the weaker answer.

WHAT GOES: app::start_new_game's pre_game_ticks loop and its sliced-progress UI, and Pass 6 background-firm generation as a separate one-shot - the firms phase 6 selects ARE the background economy.

THE KNOWN BLOCKER, written down rather than guessed at. generate_corporations APPENDS and runs BEFORE the registry loads, so phase 6 cannot vary the specialist roster at the live seam. That ordering restructure is the actual work of this item; the search itself already exists and app.cpp already calls it.

WHAT MUST NOT BE LOST. The warm start exists so play opens on a SETTLED position rather than a cold one, and the clock is rebased so play always begins at the epoch. ERAS.md carries the calendar rebase as the load-bearing, pass-independent half - play opens at epoch_year and the opening position owes the calendar nothing - and it survives whatever replaces the warm start. That paragraph is REWRITTEN, never deleted.

AND THE TRADE THIS ITEM MUST NOT MAKE. Retiring the warm start before phase 6 can genuinely hand over a settled world opens play on an UNSETTLED position, which is worse than the seconds it saves. This was refused once before on exactly that reasoning and the refusal was correct. Taking the block again is a legitimate outcome; trading correctness for a wall clock is not.

BL-812 BEARS ON THIS DIRECTLY. This item promotes phase 6 to being the only judge of the opening position, so a blind axis in its objective matters more here than it did when phase 6 merely selected alongside a warm start.

DONE WHEN: no pre_game_ticks loop remains; a world handed to play is settled by phase 6; the startup drop is measured against BL-813's figure in the release build; and ERAS.md and MARKETS.md § Background corporations describe the new source of the background economy.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the cleared board); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The game states its own generation budget on the generating screen, and the total sits in 3-6 minutes
items.design:
BEN'S TARGET, 2026-09-03: "I'm aiming to have generation take anywhere from 3-6 minutes." This item keeps that arithmetic true as the sprint moves, and makes it visible in the game rather than only in a harness.

THE VISIBLE HALF IS THE PART STILL OWED. generation_progress carries atomic budget fields and the harness tier prints a [gen budget] line, but the GENERATING SCREEN says nothing about where its wait goes. A budget nobody can see in the game is not a budget. This half was previously called delivered on a clean compile and was NOT verified by a live look - the standing rule is that a UI requirement needs a live click, so this one closes by opening the built app and looking at it.

THE ARITHMETIC TO KEEP HONEST: retiring the warm start returns most of the current wait, and the phase 6 search costs roughly +20 s of startup on its own - a regression until BL-814 removes the larger number beside it. Six candidates evaluated serially would break the budget outright; the budget closes only because they run in parallel, which makes DETERMINISM UNDER THREADING the binding constraint. A winner chosen by completion order rather than by a deterministic argmax is a non-deterministic world, and that is the one invariant this project does not bend.

THE RISK WORTH STATING: the era pass costs about FOUR TIMES its own wall clock, because everything downstream works over the regions it founded. So the cheap-looking additions are the ones to measure, not the expensive-looking ones - a budget taken off a pass's own timer is wrong by 4x.

DONE WHEN: a full generation is timed per phase in the release play build, the total sits inside 3-6 minutes, and the app itself reports the split on its generating screen - confirmed by opening the game and looking, not by a clean compile.
